implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX, aliased into ESI at 0x00641494 and used through that alias for the body's only two receiver operations; NO ordinary stack argument. implementation.return_type_note: Both exits write AL with an 8-bit instruction -- 0x006414c9 MOV AL,0x1 and 0x006414d0 XOR AL,AL -- and the only test applied to a callee's return is 0x006414b8 TEST AL,AL, also 8-bit. The machine therefore fixes the width the body touches and not a C++ spelling; the byte is what is declared. The record's canonical return claim is the register-class label 'integral_in_EAX' (abi.return_semantics, abi_derived.return.type null, register_class integral), which fixes no width at all. implementation.receiver_model: a 0x10-byte opaque byte run with no named member. Displacement 0x00 is the dispatch word this body reads at 0x006414a7; displacement 0x04 is an address this body FORMS at 0x00641496 and hands to 0x00552300, which dereferences it and reads three dwords at its +0/+4/+8 (0x0055231b, 0x00552320, 0x00552326), which is why the run is modelled to 0x10. No word is named: the machine-derived receiver record carries offsets [0] with bounds_only true, so it states where the body was seen reaching and not which member is which.
implementation.dispatch_model: the two-level table load the instruction stream shows: the receiver's word at displacement 0 (0x006414a7) is a table address, and the table's word at displacement 0x90 (0x006414a9) is the transfer target used by CALL EDX at 0x006414b6. The model names the table a local and the target a SlotTarget pointer, calls through the loaded pointer, and declares no slot INDEX, no table size and no class -- see mechanics.vtable_associations for why no index is claimable.
implementation.dependency_note: the one direct callee (0x00552300) is declared extern in the package header and defined as an observer in the package's own model test; the dispatched-to function is reached through a table word the test supplies, so no second package's header is included and this package asserts nothing about any slot's occupant beyond its own two signature facts (ECX receiver, callee-owned cleanup) which are read from 0x006417d0's bytes.

mechanics.body_shape: reserve eight bytes and save ESI; ask 0x00552300 for a status of the run at receiver+0x04; return 0 unless that status is exactly 2; load the receiver's dispatch word, take the target at table slot 0x90, and call it with the receiver in ECX and the eight-byte pair as its single argument; return 0 unless that call's AL is non-zero; AND the pair's two words and return 0 if the result is all-ones; otherwise return 1

frame_resolution.method: one linear walk of ESP through the prologue and both exits. Entry ESP is 0. SUB ESP,0x8 (0x00641490) and PUSH ESI (0x00641493) put ESP at entry-12 for the whole of the body; the direct call's own push/ADD ESP,0x4 pair is balanced by 0x0064149f; the dispatched call's single word is popped by the callee, so ESP is back at entry-12 for 0x006414bc; POP ESI and ADD ESP,0x8 land on entry+4 on both exits, which is what a bare RET consumes.
frame_resolution.corroboration: two independent agreements. (1) The address 0x006414af forms with LEA EAX,[ESP + 0x4] at ESP = entry-12, i.e. entry-8, and 0x006414bc reads the same slot with MOV EAX,[ESP + 0x4] at the same ESP: the caller reads back exactly the address it handed over, inside the eight bytes the prologue reserved. (2) 0x006417d0, the slot's occupant in the table run that agrees, writes [ECX] and [ECX+0x4] of the pointer it is given and nothing else, which are the two words this body ANDs at 0x006414bc/0x006414c0.

slots.entry-12: the saved ESI (0x00641493), popped at 0x006414cb and 0x006414d2
slots.entry-8: the pair's first word: the slot target's argument, formed at 0x006414af, read at 0x006414bc
slots.entry-4: the pair's second word: read at 0x006414c0. Never written by this body.
slots.entry+4: the return address, consumed by the bare RET. No argument word exists.

receiver_displacement.0x00: read at 0x006414a7 (MOV EDX,dword ptr [ESI]) with no displacement on the alias; it is the dispatch word, a table address, and is never dereferenced as an object by this body
receiver_displacement.0x04: formed at 0x00641496 (LEA EAX,[ESI + 0x4]) and pushed at 0x00641499. It is an ADDRESS, not a read: nothing in this body reads the receiver at 0x04, +0x08 or +0x0c. Those three words are read by 0x00552300, which dereferences the pointer it is handed (0x0055231b MOV ECX,[EAX] / 0x00552320 MOV EDX,[EAX+0x4] / 0x00552326 MOV EAX,[EAX+0x8]) and which this body calls with exactly that address.

mechanics.pair_derivation: the pair is 8 bytes at the pair's own +0 and +4, and every part of that is read off two instructions rather than assumed: 0x00641490 reserves exactly 8 bytes; 0x006414af passes the address of the first of them; 0x006414bc and 0x006414c0 read them at ESP+4 and ESP+8 with ESP at entry-12, i.e. entry-8 and entry-4, which are adjacent and inside the reservation. 0x006417d0 independently writes exactly those two words of the pointer it is given, on the one path where it returns non-zero. The body does not initialise either word, so the pair's contents are the callee's to define; the model zero-initialises the C++ object so a callee that reports success without writing is observable as (0,0) rather than as undefined behaviour, and that initialiser is a determinism aid, not a claim.
mechanics.sentinel_derivation: 0x006414c0 ANDs the two words and 0x006414c4 compares the result with -1, so the rejected case is 'both words are all-ones' and nothing else: AND yields all-ones only when both operands are. 0x006417d0 makes the same judgement on the same pair with two separate compares (CMP DWORD PTR [EAX],0xffffffff at 0x006417df and CMP DWORD PTR [EAX+0x4],0xffffffff at 0x006417e4, both branching to 0x006417806 which clears AL), which is a second witness that the pair is a pair and that all-ones in both words is the rejected case. Neither body says what the two words measure.
mechanics.control_flow: three conditional branches, all with the same absolute target inside the recovered body span: JNZ 0x006414d0 (0x006414a5), JZ 0x006414d0 (0x006414ba) and JZ 0x006414d0 (0x006414c7); plus the two unconditional terminators 0x006414cf and 0x006414d6. Four blocks, one of which (0x006414d0) is the shared failure exit. All four are modelled.
mechanics.fail_paths: 0x006414d0 XOR AL,AL is reached from all three branches and produces 0. On the first (status != 2) the pair was never formed and no dispatch happened; on the second (AL == 0) the pair was written by the callee and is not read; on the third (AND == all-ones) the pair was read. The model's three `return kFalse` sites correspond to those three in order, and the model test drives all three.
mechanics.globals: none. The complete 30-instruction body names no data-segment address. The absolute operands in it are the direct call target 0x00552300 and the three branch targets 0x006414d0, all of which are code.

vtable_associations.why_no_slot_index_is_claimed: one fixed displacement cannot be +0x80 in one run and +0x74 in another, so the two groups are either secondary tables in a multiple-inheritance layout or the record's table starts are off by four bytes, and this record cannot say which. Independently, this binary carries no MSVC RTTI (the byte before the run at 0x013ff648 is the float constant 0x3f000000, not a complete-object locator), so no index 0 can be located and no ordinal can be counted from the top of a table. The model therefore states the displacement 0x90, which is read straight out of the instruction, and nothing else.
vtable_associations.slot_occupant_corroboration: 0x006417d0's own body is the corroboration for the slot's SIGNATURE rather than for the slot's identity: it takes the receiver in ECX, takes one stack word, writes [ECX] and [ECX+0x4] of it, tests the same all-ones-in-both-words condition this body ANDs for, and returns 0x1/0x0 in AL with RET 0x4. So the model test's slot observer is a behavioural stand-in for it, and the model's `SlotTarget` type is that signature.

mechanics.return_semantics_machine: one byte in AL, produced on four of the four paths. 0x006414c9 MOV AL,0x1 on the surviving path; 0x006414d0 XOR AL,AL on the shared failure path reached from all three branches. Both are 8-bit operations and the body clears nothing else, so bits 8..31 of EAX are dead: on the surviving path they carry bits 8..31 of the AND result, and on the three failing paths they carry whatever the last thing to run in EAX left there (0x00552300's status word, the slot call's own return word, or the AND result). The model returns the byte and asserts nothing about the rest; the record lists no caller for this VA at all (all six xrefs are data references from pointer runs), so nothing in this repository observes those bits.

semantics.shape: a three-way-gated predicate returning one byte
semantics.gate_2: the slot at table displacement 0x90, called on the receiver with a pointer to an 8-byte frame pair, must return a non-zero low byte
semantics.gate_3: the AND of the pair's two words must not be 0xffffffff
semantics.on_failure: every failing gate lands on one shared block at 0x006414d0, which clears AL and returns. The three gates are independent: none implies either of the others, and the model test drives each of them with the other two satisfied.
semantics.ownership: the body performs no reference acquisition or release. It reads one pointer out of the receiver, hands two addresses to callees, and writes nothing to the receiver at all -- the model test asserts that as a byte-level fact over a receiver with a sentinel tail, not as a claim about the struct.
semantics.not_claimed: what the two words of the pair measure, what 0x00552300's four return values mean, what the dispatch word is beyond being a table address, and whether any of this is reachable in the shipped game. The body is a virtual entry in a Sporepedia asset-data table family and its name is not established by any record here.

unresolved_questions: The committed record's body span is four bytes short. ghidra_function reports body_end 0x006414cf, size 64 and 25 instructions, and all three conditional branches in it target 0x006414d0 -- outside that span. The image shows the body continuing to 0x006414d6 and the live decompilation follows it. Whether the right fix is to extend the recorded body, to split the failure block into its own function, or to leave it, is a decision for the integrator and for whatever owns the evidence pack; this package reconstructed the body the bytes show and says so in function_extent. It is also why CONTROL FLOW cannot pass for this target: the check bounds the body with the committed listing's own addresses, and no source shape can change that.

Why are this body's slot entries at +0x80 in three tables and at +0x74 in two others? A single fixed displacement cannot be both. Either the two groups are primary and secondary tables of a multiple-inheritance hierarchy (in which case the object's address within itself differs by four bytes between them) or the record's table starts are off by four bytes for one group. Nothing in this repository settles it, and no slot index is claimed anywhere in this package because of it.

What is the function at slot displacement 0x90? Three tables hold 0x006417d0 there, and that function's shape (one stack word, writes two words, rejects all-ones in both, returns AL) matches everything this body does with the call -- but the transfer target is a run-time value in EDX and this body never names it, so a table whose 0x90 entry is a DIFFERENT function of the same signature would be indistinguishable here. The model calls through the loaded pointer and the test supplies its own observer, which is the honest shape for a dispatch.

What do the pair's two words measure? Nothing in either body says. 0x006417d0 fetches them through its own receiver+0x1c and rejects all-ones in both, which is consistent with a range, an extent or an index pair, and the body ANDs them rather than comparing either, which is consistent with 'both ends unset'. No name is used.

What do 0x00552300's four return values (0x0, 0x1, 0x2, and the word it loads at [EBP-0x30]) mean, and why does this body want the one at 0x0055241f -- the arm its listing takes after 0x005523f9 MOVZX EAX,AL / 0x005523fc TEST EAX,EAX falls through to when its own 0x00550970 call returns zero? The body tests only 2 and names only 2. The callee is not owned by this package and nothing about its internals is asserted beyond its convention, its pointer argument and the four values it can return.

What is the receiver's real extent? 0x10 is where this body and 0x00552300 were observed reaching; the object may be larger, and the three dwords 0x00552300 reads through receiver+0x04 are themselves opaque. No member is named for any of them.

Is the pair's uninitialised state ever observable? The body reads the pair only after the slot call reported a non-zero AL, and the one slot occupant this evidence identifies always writes both words on that path -- but the body cannot know that of a table it has not seen, so a table whose 0x90 entry returns non-zero without writing the pair would make this body read uninitialised frame bytes. That is a property of the machine, not of the reconstruction; the model zero-initialises the object and says so in the .cpp.

The declared return type is std::uint8_t and the record's canonical return claim is the string 'integral_in_EAX'. Those do not agree textually, which is why RETURN SEMANTICS is a WARN and not a PASS. The machine fixes the width the body writes and tests (8 bits in AL, at 0x006414c9, 0x006414d0 and 0x006414b8) and no record narrows the register class to a width; a C++ spelling that satisfied the string comparison would be a fiction, so the byte is declared and the disagreement is reported instead of gamed. The original source almost certainly said `bool` (the MOV AL,1 / XOR AL,AL idiom is what MSVC emits for it) but that is INFERRED, not machine-fixed, and the model does not claim it.
